ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The image lists four substances and their structures: methanol (methanol), propane (propane), ethene (ethylene), and ethanal (acetaldehyde). The methanol structure has a hydroxyl group -OH; the ethanal structure has a polar carbonyl group C=O; propane and ethene contain only carbon-hydrogen bonds and belong to nonpolar hydrocarbons. According to the rule of "like dissolves like," water is a polar substance, and small-molecule polar substances are more likely to be miscible with water, while nonpolar hydrocarbons are usually not easily miscible with water. The question stem has already given that ethanal is one of them, so the other substance most likely to be miscible with water is methanol.
